title: Herb Crusted Middle Eastern Pork Rib Tagine
description: An earthy, anti-inflammatory-friendly tagine featuring tender pork back ribs slow-cooked in warming spices, topped with a crunchy herb crust and brightened with tangy nuka-pickle.
instructions: Rub the pork back ribs thoroughly with one tablespoon of ras el hanout, turmeric, salt, and one tablespoon of olive oil.
Heat one tablespoon of olive oil in the base of a ceramic tagine over medium heat and sear the ribs until browned on all sides.
Remove the ribs temporarily, then saute the shallots, smashed garlic, and grated ginger in the remaining tagine juices for three minutes.
Pour in the bone broth, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the ceramic vessel.
Return the ribs to the tagine, cover with the conical lid, and simmer on low heat for ninety minutes until the meat is tender.
While the ribs cook, combine the chopped parsley, mint, crushed almonds, remaining ras el hanout, and last tablespoon of olive oil to create the herb crust mixture.
Uncover the tagine, scatter the diced nuka-pickle over the ribs, and spread the herb-almond crust mixture evenly across the top of the meat.
Place the uncovered tagine under a preheated oven broiler for five minutes until the herb crust is fragrant and crunchy.
